summary: Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1946) under Hajime Tanabe. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1959–1976) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1977–1988), and joined the Japan Academy in 1995.

Yoshinori Yasuda (1946–2026) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Ritsumeikan University and Tohoku University. He served as Professor Emeritus at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–2012) and as professor at Tohoku University (~2012–2014).

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a sinology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and under Paul Demiéville (~1957–1959), later serving as an assistant librarian at Kyoto University from ~1953 to 1984.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi (1886–1966) was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1907 to 1910 and held a post at Tohoku University from ~1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda (b. 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under Ariane Macdonald, Rolf Alfred Stein, and Shoju Inaba. His career includes posts at CNRS and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University (1965–1972), the University of Tokyo (1972–1982), and Rissho University (~1982–1989).

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He later held posts at Kyoto University, as Chinese literature department head at Nagoya University (1955–1977), and at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1979–1986).

Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held appointments at Columbia University, serving as professor in 1966 and until 1983 as associate professor of Japanese and religion.
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He has held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshitsugu Sawai (b. 1951) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and John B. Carman. He was a professor and dean of human studies at Tenri University (~1984–2017).

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2006) and lecturer (attested 2015), and is attested at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (2026).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe (b. 1947) works in computational studies and Tibetology. He completed his D.Sc. at Tohoku University, where he served as research associate (1975–1990) and professor at the Institute for Materials Research (1990–2012), later becoming professor emeritus in 2012.

Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University (~1935–1939), where he later served as professor (~1968–1986), and directed the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1977–1987).

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, and later taught at Rowan University (attested 2007, 2018).
Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and held a post there from approximately 1891 to 1898.

Yozo Taniyama (b. 1972) works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tohoku University (~1991–1996), he held positions at Sophia University (~2000–2004), St. Thomas University, Japan (~2004–2007), Shitennoji University (~2007–2012), and Tohoku University (~2012).
Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Tsui completed master's studies at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and pursued doctoral research supervised by Natasha Heller, also studying under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, later teaching at National Central University (~2001–2011).
